text: A SAFETYNET briefing room. Netherton by the screen, HaX with the file open, and a man in a lab coat half-buried in a laptop he built himself.
Agent 0x00. This is Operation Cyber Arsenal.
Zero Day Syndicate used to sell exploits to whoever paid. Now they choose the targets first.
That is a line I do not let anyone cross. You are going in.
HaX runs you, Nightshade the technical side. Listen to both.
Morning. Whatever they've built, I'll take it apart from here. You just get me close to it.
HaX. The floor's yours.
Right. Zero Day Syndicate. You heard of them?
Zero Day runs behind a real pentest firm -- WhiteHat Security Services. Legitimate audits by day. An exploit marketplace in the back rooms.
They don't run the attacks. They arm the cells that do.
Ransomware Incorporated. Critical Mass. Others we haven't confirmed. Zero Day is their common supplier.
You worked St. Catherine's last month. The hospital that went dark.
The ransomware ran on a ProFTPD backdoor. That exploit didn't come from the crew who deployed it.
They did. An invoice turned up at St. Catherine's with Zero Day's name on the sale. Now we want their side of it.
They sold it as a product. Twenty-five thousand on the invoice, healthcare premium already built into the price.
They knew, and they billed for knowing. That's the case we're building. And there's a Phase 2 behind it.
Three things, then. One: get inside and clone Victoria Sterling's executive keycard. She's the front's CEO, and she runs this end of the cell for 0day.
Two: after hours, get onto their training network and pull the flags. Recon, the services, and the legacy distcc box where their records sit.
Three: the physical paper trail. Client roster, the catalogue, anything naming St. Catherine's or Phase 2.
Ask me whatever you need before you go in.
Victoria Sterling. Founded WhiteHat in 2010, former conference speaker, respected researcher on the record.
On our side of the record she runs the front and answers to 0day and the Architect. Her sign-off name is Sable.
No. She runs the shop floor. 0day leads the cell, the Architect coordinates the network.
Her name's on the invoices. That's why she's the one you can reach.
Two stages. Reception first. The receptionist's badge opens the conference area. Weak defaults, so it cracks in seconds. Talk to her and lean in by her lanyard.
Then Sterling's executive card in the meeting. Custom keys, so it's Darkside -- about half a minute.
Your moment's at the whiteboard. Stand close and keep her talking while it reads.
Capture and replay. Her card broadcasts, we copy it, we wear it. Same trick they use on us.
One day it'll be our badge somebody clones. Remember how easy it was.
Last time, a card meant getting it off somebody. This time you just stand next to it.
Picks for anything keyed, the cloner for anything carded. No PIN cracker this time. Nightshade still has ours in pieces from St. Catherine's.
Play the curious recruit. She loves talking about the work. The cloner is passive until you trigger it.
In the server room you'll find their training lab: an isolated VM network, reachable only from a terminal in that room. It's where they rehearse exploits before they sell them.
Map it, work the services, and get to the legacy distcc box. That's where the operational logs live.
Recon, FTP, the web host's price list, then distcc for the logs. The distcc one is the case.
Four flags. Submit each at the drop-site terminal in the server room -- it sends them to me.
You're a freelance pentester Sterling's looking at as a recruit. Small firms, drawn to the grey-market side. That's the profile that gets you a meeting.
Entry is a conference-room meeting this afternoon. After that the building empties and you come back for the real work.
After dark. Most staff gone, a guard on patrol in the executive wing. That's your window.
Before you go in -- how do you want to play it?
Your call.
Good. Zero Day invoices everything, so somewhere in that building St. Catherine's is on paper. Bring me the paper.
Thorough takes time, though, and there's a guard on nights. Don't let him find you reading.
Listen. Every life St. Catherine's lost, it lost to something Zero Day sold.
Good. Keep your head down in there.
WhiteHat Security, Callaghan Square, Cardiff. I'm on comms the whole time. The drop-site terminal in the server room takes your flags and sends them straight to me.
And one more thing. Come back in one piece.
Meet Sterling, clone her card, then come back after dark. Go.
Last look. Once you're out, the search team has that building.
The server room safe's still shut, for one.
Go on, then. She's not leaving her desk tonight.
Still in there. That search team's getting restless.
The server room safe's still shut, for one.
Side door, two minutes. Don't use the lobby.
Leave her to us.
SAFETYNET headquarters. The morning after WhiteHat Security.
There you are. Sit down before you fall down.
The network first. All four flags, and the distcc logs are the case.
